name: Vesk Veilclaw
tagline: Dragonborn monk, wayfarer and asker of questions
intro: You've come off the road into the biggest puzzle on the Sword Coast. A city this size is all locked doors and sealed letters, and nobody here has decided what you are yet.

sections.heading: You know your own people
extra: In the marshes, your black scales told people everything about you. Here, most people couldn't tell you what scale color is supposed to mean, which makes a refreshing change.

sections.heading: You know the city's shadows
sections.because: Wayfarer background · Insight proficiency · Thieves' Tools
sections.lead: A wayfarer learns fast who to trust, and you read people well enough to spot the ones who are working an angle.

sections.heading: You know where travelers end up
extra: Monastery training on slick stones has left you comfortable where most people aren't: Dock Ward rooftops are close enough to cross for someone nimble.

lists.heading: Tools and languages
items: **Thieves' Tools:** locks are puzzles. In Waterdeep, opening one that isn't yours is a crime, and the Watch won't care that you were curious.
**Flute:** enough to earn a meal in a tavern that's short of musicians.
**Draconic:** see above. Wizards and old books use its script.
**Elvish:** you learned it copying old texts, and you can read what most city folk can't. Waterdeep's elves are few, but its libraries hold plenty of elven writing.

story: You grew up in Clan Veilclaw, in fog-choked marshes among drowned ruins, hearing that your scales told the world everything about you. You never believed it.

You trained at the House of the Drowned Lantern, a half-sunken monastery whose Abbess taught that shadow is where you stand to protect the light. You were never a silent monk. The Abbess sent you off to be a useful one.
You carry a notebook of unanswered questions. Waterdeep should add a few pages.
